title: Smart Billboard In Bengaluru Displays Drivers' Pending Fines In Real Time: 'Need A Pothole Updater Too' | Bengaluru-news News - News18
text: Bengaluru has now taken traffic monitoring to a whole new level. A post circulating online shows how the city police, in collaboration with Cars24, have installed an AI-powered billboard at Trinity Circle. This high-tech screen is connected with cameras and the VAHAN database to keep an eye on vehicles within a 100-meter range. Within just ten seconds, it can detect if a driver has any pending traffic challans or an expired pollution certificate, instantly displaying the details on the large screen. While many view it as a smart initiative to remind people about their dues, some argue that the authorities could have used it more effectively. Suggestions include displaying the number of potholes on the road along with their repair status in real time. Others feel the billboard would be more useful if it focused on alerting about traffic violators rather than publicly displaying pending fines and dues. Bengaluru Launches AI-Powered Traffic Billboard As per Money Control, Gajendra Jangid, co-founder & CMO, Cars24, said, “We are not reminding people to clear challans or update documents. We’re reminding them that every act of responsibility on the road, no matter how small, is what keeps an entire city alive. Safety doesn’t come from systems alone; it comes from choices. And the road is the one place where your choices instantly touch thousands of lives." “The AI-powered billboard pilot aims to improve road safety by making drivers immediately aware of their pending fines and vehicle compliance status, which will encourage responsible behaviour on the roads," a senior police officer said. Social Media Users Share Ideas And Concerns Reacting to the post, a user suggested, “Can they put a billboard opposite to offices of BBMP Engineers, commissioners, houses of MLA about potholes everywhere in Bengaluru? Just a small act to show a mirror to their outstanding contribution." Another shared, “Government is shaking people down. Probably the only way to get people to pay." “Need a pothole updater and resolved billboard as well," a comment read. An individual jokingly stated, “That board is not sufficient. It will display overflow/server error shortly." Another mentioned, “It can also display if any ambulance is coming in that route." One more added, “Let’s improvise this. BTP should put up cameras on one ways and junctions and capture and flash wrong side drivers as well as would be fine. This wrong-side driving issue will get resolved in a quarter." Traffic Fines In Bengaluru Between August 23 and September 12, Bengaluru traffic police reportedly collected Rs 106 crore in fines from over 36 lakh cases. The city has over one crore registered vehicles, with around 30,000 traffic violations recorded daily. From January to August 2025, 45 lakh violations were documented.
